title: Per-GPU calibration harness, profile signatures, and canary publisher for model onboarding
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a deterministic per-device calibration harness and a signed performance-profile publishing pipeline that enables safe model onboarding and version pinning across GPU SKUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300). The goal is to replace ad-hoc CSV artifacts with canonical, signed profile blobs and an automated canary publisher that validates profiles on representative hardware before making them discoverable to runtime routing and the Console.

Background: We currently rely on manually-curated performance profiles and one-off benchmark artifacts. This makes it hard to (1) ensure profile authenticity across releases, (2) gate profile publication with repeatable per-device checks, and (3) attach metadata required for automated fallbacks and pinning. Onboarding new model versions often requires manual triage when latency/cost regressions appear on specific SKUs.

Scope/Goals:
- Define a canonical profile schema (profile version, model id, model sha, quantization tag, sequence-length buckets, batch-throughput table, tail-latency percentiles, memory headroom, kernel-hint) and include a signed signature block for integrity.
- Build a per-GPU calibration harness that runs short representative workloads (synthetic and real prompt subset) on A100, H100, L40S, MI300 to produce stable latency/throughput numbers and a calibration vector used by the runtime (KV cache warmup multiplier, preferred batch size, kernel selection hints).
- Implement an automated canary publisher service: it deploys candidate profiles to a small canary fleet, runs an acceptance suite (latency SLO tests, regression detection against pinned baseline, memory/oom checks), and only promotes signed profiles to the public catalog if checks pass.
- Add CI gating: profile artifacts must be produced by the harness (artifact hash) and accompany model onboarding PRs. CI runs limited-canary on cloud-backed test hardware and blocks merge on regressions.
- Expose metadata in the Console and SDK: model onboarding UI shows per-SKU deltas vs pinned baseline, last-calibrated timestamp, and signs/validator ID.

Acceptance criteria:
- A canonical profile JSON schema documented in Confluence with examples for each GPU SKU.
- Harness implementation that produces repeatable calibration vectors (stddev < 3% across 10 runs) for A100/H100/L40S/MI300 on our lab fleets.
- Canary publisher that runs the acceptance suite and publishes signed profiles to the catalog with an audit trail.
- CI checks integrated into the model-onboarding pipeline; at least one onboarding PR demonstrates the end-to-end flow (artifact produced, canary validated, profile published).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We sign profiles to protect against accidental mismatch and enable cross-team trust; signing adds complexity in key management but prevents silent regressions due to stale artifacts. Integration will reuse the existing KMS workflow (runtime-1.20).
- Canary sizing: small canary fleet (2 nodes per SKU) minimizes cost but may miss rare tail regressions; we'll run an extended pre-publish window for high-risk models (LLMs > 70B).
- Schema verbosity vs ease-of-use: prioritize explicit fields for kernel hints and sequence distribution to let runtime make strong routing decisions; extra metadata increases profile size but avoids re-running heavy benchmarks on the serving side.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Per-GPU+Profile+Schema+and+Canary+Workflow
- Design doc (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1HwProfileDesign
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Canary dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Canary/Per-GPU-Canary
- Example profile for A100: https://storage.redwood.ai/profiles/ENG-18732/a100-v1.json

Rollout plan:
1) Merge harness code and schema (runtime-1.22 branch) behind a feature flag.
2) Run calibration on internal lab fleets for all SKUs; validate repeatability and tune acceptance thresholds.
3) Enable canary publisher for low-risk models (<=7B) and monitor for one week.
4) Expand to mid/high-risk models with extended canary windows, then set as default for onboarding.

Risk and mitigation:
- False positives: acceptance thresholds too tight can block valid profiles. Mitigation: tiered thresholds and manual override with mandatory audit.
- Key compromise: signing key leakage would be serious. Mitigation: use HSM-protected KMS keys and rotation policy, restrict publisher service identity.
- Hardware availability: limited MI300 capacity could delay canaries. Mitigation: use simulated calibration vectors for low-risk cases and require physical run only for release candidates.

Next steps:
- Diego to finalize schema and open RFC (due 2025-11-12).
- Dev work to implement harness (ETA 3 weeks) and short PR for CI integration.
- Schedule lab time for MI300 runs and confirm stability window.

For reviewers: Please focus on the schema validity (are we missing fields needed by the runtime?), the suggested acceptance checks (latency SLOs and regression thresholds), and whether the canary sizing is sufficient for production safety.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Ava Chen: Created ticket; initial problem statement and high-level plan. Added prototype PR link. Assigned to Diego.
2025-11-07 - Diego Morales: Posted first draft of canonical profile schema in the design doc. Requesting feedback from runtime and infra. Asking for guidance on kernel-hint naming conventions.

2025-11-10 - Priya Nair (runtime): Reviewed schema and suggested adding `memory_headroom_percent` and `kv_cache_warmup_seconds`. Also requested an explicit `quantization_compat` field with allowed values.
2025-11-12 - Diego Morales: Updated schema based on Priya's feedback and pushed RFC to Confluence. Scheduled design review for 2025-11-14.
2025-11-14 - Design review notes: Agreed on schema fields; decided to include `profile_ttl` to force re-calibration cadence. Action: add TTL enforcement to canary publisher.
2025-11-20 - Diego Morales: Prototype harness runs on A100 lab fleet. Initial results: median latency stabilizes but 95th has 5% jitter. Tuned warmup and saw 95th drop to ~2.8% stddev across 10 runs.

2025-11-27 - QA: Canary acceptance suite created (latency SLO, throughput delta, OOM checks). Hooked suite into CI for PR #2345. CI run failed due to memory regression on one MI300 node - investigating.
2025-11-30 - Infra: MI300 node had a driver mismatch; after update, harness re-ran and passed. Added driver version check to the acceptance suite.
2025-12-03 - Diego Morales: Implemented signature block using KMS sign API. Added audit-trail metadata (publisher identity, commit SHA, canary run id).
2025-12-08 - Ava Chen: Marking ticket In Progress. Next: expand canary fleet to staging and add Console UI card for per-SKU deltas. Due date set to 2025-12-15.
